metadata.title: Core Scientific Q2 revenue doubles as AMD deal expands AI leasing pipeline: Q2 Earnings

content.text:
Core Scientific (NASDAQ: CORZ) reported $164.2 million in second-quarter revenue on Tuesday, a 109% increase from $78.6 million a year earlier, with colocation becoming its biggest business. The data center operator also unveiled an AMD partnership that has the potential to support as much as 2.5 GW of leasable capacity across five sites.
The earnings call came on the same day as the firm announced a 500 MW deal with chip producer AMD, with a base contract of $14 billion. Core Scientific says the deal has room to grow to a full pipeline of 2.5 GW
Colocation produced $136.7 million of quarterly revenue, compared with $10.6 million in the same period last year. Total gross profit reached $70 million, up from $5 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased to $41.1 million from $28.5 million.
Core Scientific finished the quarter with 395 MW of billing capacity, compared with 225 MW at the close of the first quarter. By mid-July, billing had climbed to 437 MW, a level Core Scientific linked to roughly $635 million in average annualized colocation GAAP revenue.

AMD agreements expand the leasing pipeline
Core Scientific said total leased customer power capacity had reached about 1.1 GW, representing more than $24 billion in potential contracted revenue over the relevant contract terms. The AMD-backed plan adds a potential path toward 2.5 GW of leasable capacity, though that larger figure is not fully contracted.
The initial AMD agreements cover about 530 MW across five sites under 15-year terms. Core Scientific estimated that those contracts could generate more than $14 billion in base revenue over their duration.
Those figures describe potential long-term contracted revenue rather than revenue recognized during the second quarter. Construction schedules, financing and the delivery of power and equipment will determine when capacity enters service and begins contributing to reported revenue.
Core Scientific recorded $797.5 million in capital expenditures during the quarter, more than double the $389.2 million spent in the first quarter and up from $121.3 million a year earlier.
Warrant accounting drives the net loss
Core Scientific posted a net loss of $1.155 billion, or $3.32 per basic and diluted share, versus a $936.8 million loss in the second quarter of 2025. The loss was mainly the result of a $1.046 billion remeasurement of warrants and contingent value rights as Core Scientific's share price rose.
The company reported an operating loss of $78.5 million and interest expense of $23.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA excludes warrant revaluations, interest and several other noncash or startup-related costs, leaving the non-GAAP measure at $41.1 million.
